blocks.text: Do smart appliances make the home a better place? Here are quick recommendations to making the home maintenance easier. From practical tech to robot vacuum guides, we got them!

There was a time back in September where the metro experienced relentless rain and bouts of sunshine. That last hurrah of Q3 is a wildcard for many Filipinos because we always expect the worst unpredictable weather during that time.

This year, we discovered molds in our cabinets in the dirty kitchen due to wild fluctuations in humidity. It was at that time I noticed huge order spikes in dehumidifiers from Shopee so I gave it a spin and found this 12L dehumidifier from Carrier. It’s perfect for small rooms and single apartments. I discovered that the dehumidifier does more than just removing molds.

On the first few days we ran the dehumidifier twice a day with all the doors closed. Both sessions of roughly 3 hours filled the 12L tank twice to the brim. But what I also discovered was that it also makes for a good dryer for clothes fresh from the washing machine.

I’ve seen some smart washing machines with built-in dryers but the main complaint of this tech is that the drying function can use up a lot of electricity. Lo and behold, with the dehumidifier, we were able to dry clothes faster.

The dehumidifier has an added boon for my situation as I own a 3D printer. One of the most important commandments of filament maintenance is to keep humidity low else the filament prints will spaghetti, wasting both money and time. Although these filament spools are kept in individual packaging with desiccant, it doesn’t hurt to control the overall room humidity to levels below 40%.

I own several robot vacuums at home, from several brands, across the better part of a decade. But this one from Dyson, the spot+scrub Ai, is noteworthy because it comes with three receptacles in the home dock: one for solid dirt, one for clean water, and another for dirty water.

When buying a robot vacuum, at least look for one with a mop function. Just having the sweepers won’t cut it, especially if you want to really clean dirt that sticks to the floor. But if you can spare the extra cash, do get one like this unit: a vacuum function that cleans and deposits wet and solid dirt without you having to change the mop all the time.

I remember the first time we used this. The water from the roller was really dirty, almost soot black. As time passed, it gradually shifted to lighter shades of gray which means the constant cleaning really makes a difference. The only time I had to manually take over was to empty the dirty water tank and replace the clean one with fresh water.
A smart refrigerator (it’s not what you think)
OK hold your horses. In the world of smart appliances, why would a refrigerator with an app make sense to me?

How many times have you woken up, gone to the kitchen and realized the bottom freezer door was left open by your kids? This has happened twice to me in ten years, resulting in having to repair the compressor (which isn’t cheap!).

A smart refrigerator, such as the space saving ones from Midea has an app (MSmartHome) that notifies you if the ref door has been left open. It also sends another notification when the door has been shut. This has been an anxiety suppressor for months now because I no longer need to worry if my kids accidentally leave the ref door open, especially when I am out on a trip.
